purpose: PET4D provides a DICOM plugin for loading ECG-gated, dynamic, and static PET series into 3D Slicer as sequences or volumes in SUV (SUVbw, SUVlbm, SUVbsa) or Bq/ml while preserving frame timing, tracer, and decay metadata. It also provides interactive modules for nuclear medicine researchers and clinicians to review/edit dynamic frames, perform frame-by-frame motion correction, register dynamic PET to CT/MR, and perform regional and voxel-wise kinetic modeling (1TC, 2TC, Patlak, Logan, SRTM, SUVR).
summary: PET4D is a well-structured, self-contained 3D Slicer extension for loading, reviewing, motion-correcting, registering, and kinetically modeling gated and dynamic PET series. It relies solely on Slicer's bundled Python/C++ libraries (numpy, scipy, SimpleITK, pydicom, BRAINSFit), performs no external network requests or package installations, is licensed under MIT, and has a valid CMake build configuration and catalog entry. 🟢 Recommend merge.

safety.rationale: Inspected the Python modules and searched across the entire repository for network calls, subprocess execution, dynamic code execution, and file operations. There is no network communication, telemetry, external binary download, command injection, or unsafe deserialization; file writes occur only via explicit user file dialogs or cleaned-up temporary directories for local DICOM database import.

environment.rationale: Inspected all module scripts and library modules (`DICOMGatedDynamicPET/*.py`, `DICOMGatedDynamicPET/DICOMGatedDynamicPETLib/*.py`). The extension uses only Slicer-bundled packages (`numpy`, `scipy`, `SimpleITK`, `pydicom`, `vtk`, `qt`, `ctk`) without any `pip_install` calls, PyTorch usage, or invasive global monkey-patching.

packaging.rationale: Inspected `PET4D.json`, root `CMakeLists.txt`, and `DICOMGatedDynamicPET/CMakeLists.txt`. All 6 scripted modules, all 18 library scripts under `DICOMGatedDynamicPETLib/`, and all icon/image resources exist and are properly installed via `slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule`, and `EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA"` matches `build_dependencies: []`.

license.rationale: Inspected `LICENSE`, which grants clear distribution permission under the permissive MIT License (Copyright (c) 2026 Burak Demir). No restricted third-party weights or proprietary binaries are bundled or downloaded.

soundness.rationale: Inspected the module classes, logic, custom widgets, and test suite (`Testing/test_*.py` and module self-tests). The code follows Slicer conventions cleanly, manages VTK observers and temporary helper nodes on scene/session close, reports errors gracefully, and uses progress dialogs for multi-frame operations.

utility.rationale: Inspected `README.md` and module implementations. The extension fills an important gap for 4D/dynamic and ECG-gated PET workflows in Slicer (frame-aware DICOM loading, frame editing, motion correction, co-registration, and compartment/graphical kinetic modeling), includes a clear clinical disclaimer, and provides comprehensive documentation and unit/self-tests.

findings.title: Prepending module directory to sys.path at module import
findings.explanation: Each scripted module (`DICOMGatedDynamicPET.py`, `DynamicPETEditor.py`, `DynamicPETModeling.py`, `DynamicPETMotionCorrection.py`, `DynamicPETRegistration.py`, `GatedDynamicPETSettings.py`) inserts its module directory at the front of `sys.path` if not already present. Slicer already adds scripted module directories to `sys.path` or supports importing helper packages placed alongside the module script, and the modules/packages here use distinct names (`DICOMGatedDynamicPETLib`, `DynamicPET*`), so the risk of name collisions with standard or bundled libraries is very low.
findings.suggestion: Rely on Slicer's standard module path handling or append rather than prepend to `sys.path` if needed for standalone testing.

not_checked: Runtime execution of tests and interactive GUI layouts inside a running 3D Slicer instance.
